title: LADIES WATCH
findings: Ladies quartz-style dress watch, round gilt case with Cartier Must Vendome-style ball lugs, black dial with diagonal gold band, two hands, no numerals. Small three-line logo at 12 too small to read even enlarged. Old paper shop tag marked 99.50 attached, suggests old shop stock. No case back photo, no maker confirmed.
condition: Black leather strap cracked and worn through at holes, gilt case appears OK, dial band slightly speckled.
reason: Unbranded-looking gilt fashion watch, dial logo unreadable, no evidence of a collectable maker.

interest.note: Gilt ladies dress watch, Vendome-style lugs, black/gold dial, maker unreadable, old shop tag 99.50; no case back shown.

title: 2 FRANKLIN MINT COLLECTOR KNIVES
findings: Two Franklin Mint collector lock-back pocket knives with printed wildlife scenes (whitetail deer, grizzly bear) and cast brass-tone bolsters with stag and bear heads, in black zip pouches marked 'Knives'.
condition: Pouch of the bear knife cracked and flaking; knives appear unused.
reason: Mass-produced Franklin Mint collector knives, low resale ($15-30 each).

title: ROYAL MINIATURE CORONATION COACH & HORSES - MADE BY LESNEY
findings: Small diecast silver/gilt finish State Coronation coach with eight white horses and four red-coated riders, about 11cm long. This is the small common 1953 Lesney coronation coach, not the large rare Moko Lesney version. No base visible.
condition: Paint chips to horses, light wear to silvered coach; appears complete.
reason: Common small Lesney 1953 coronation coach, typically $20-40.

title: 2 PENCILS INCL 1934 ENGRAVED
findings: Two propelling pencils. 1) Octagonal engine-turned gold-coloured propelling pencil with clip, engraved 'From Max Xmas 1934' (last digit could be 7); small two-line stamp near the clip ring is not legible enough to confirm 9ct or a maker (could be 'MADE IN ENGLAND' or a rolled gold mark). 2) Celluloid red/white/blue striped Coronation pencil with crown finial, embossed 'CORONATION ... JUNE 1953'.
condition: Light wear, gilt rubbed on gold pencil clip; coronation pencil small mark to celluloid.
reason: 1930s engine-turned propelling pencil may be solid gold (stamp unreadable) and coronation 1953 pencil is collectable; worth checking marks in hand.
marks_read: 'From Max Xmas 1934'; 'CORONATION ... JUNE 1953'; clip stamp illegible

title: SHIBUMI HOLLOW GROUND HUNTING KNIFE IN SHEATH
findings: Fixed blade hunting knife with upswept trailing-point blade, filework/scalloped spine, brass bolster, ribbed brown composite handle with leather lanyard, in brown suede/leather riveted sheath. Blade etched 'SHIBUMI' over 'L. Henson, Maker' (title says Shibumi hollow ground). Quick search found nothing on this maker; possibly a small custom or import mark.
condition: Blade tarnished and scratched with some staining; sheath worn and marked with lot sticker.
reason: Maker-marked hunting knife (Shibumi, L. Henson Maker), knives with maker marks have a collector market; maker unidentified.
